title: Let agents amend a booked trip without touching it

blocks.text: A travel agency's agents change a booked trip by editing an amendment of it: they drop a leg, add one, move a passenger to another seat, add a bag. The amendment replaces the booking only when the customer confirms it. Last week a customer who never confirmed anything found their return flight gone from the booking and a bicycle on their first leg.
`Itinerary` and its `Leg` already hold a trip. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Itinerary.java`:

items: `Leg.copy()`: a leg like this one, for an amendment;

blocks.text: When you're done, an amendment starts as the booked trip, the agent can make any of those changes to it, and none of them shows up on the booking. About five lines in total.

cases.says: an amendment is a separate itinerary with the booking's reference and the same legs, seats and bags, in order
a leg removed from the amendment is still on the booked trip
a seat changed on one of the amendment's legs leaves the booked leg's seat as it was
a bag added to one of the amendment's legs is not added to the booked leg
the agent can add a leg to the amendment, and the booked trip keeps its own legs

origin.section: A Copy Is Only as Deep as the Code That Made It

concepts: Assigning a reference copies the reference, so two variables reach one object and a change through either is seen through both.
An independent copy copies every mutable level, nested collections included, or makes the lower levels immutable.
A copy made with new ArrayList<>(list) is a new list of the same element objects, so a change to an element reaches the original.
